generated_note: Typed links for the controlled-vocabulary and interpretation-guidelines records authored to back the ISO 26262 Part 1 and Part 10 entries of docs/artifacts/governance/coverage-plan.json. Generated into the canonical registry as a new file rather than edited into an existing one, so the existing registries' 547 links are unchanged and this file can be diffed against them independently. No reviewed_by link is declared here: this pass adds no review record, and a reviewed_by link whose endpoint is not in any review record's reviewed_ids would put the two sources out of agreement and trip the acceptance gate. change_suspect_status is false on every link here because each link was authored against the endpoint revisions it names and no endpoint has advanced past them; the corpus's own link validator derives that field rather than trusting the stored one, and stored true is reported as a contradiction when the derived value is false.

links.rationale: The `item` and `item definition` entries in this vocabulary are defined from this record: it is the only item definition in the corpus, and its item_name, item_purpose and boundary rationale are what those two entries describe.

The hazard, hazardous event, malfunctioning behaviour and operational situation entries are defined from this record, because it is the corpus's only populated hazard artefact and because the two profiles' copies of it differ, which is the reading the hazardous event entry records.

The `safety function` entry cites this record's prose use of the phrase, and the absence of a safety_function artefact type is a finding this vocabulary records against it. The dependency is on the usage, not on any technical claim the record makes.

Every term convention this guidelines record relies on is stated in the vocabulary record and is referenced rather than restated, so that the two records cannot drift apart silently. The guidelines record names the eight it uses in conventions_taken_from_the_vocabulary_record.

GDL-006 reads the gap-declaration convention off this record's own why-no-record-was-created reasoning, which is the corpus's clearest statement of the rule against closing a gap by inventing a record.

The guidelines record supplies the reading conventions under which the safety case skeleton's claims and arguments are to be read; the skeleton's own release recommendation authorises nothing and this record does not change that.
